text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- A government bond issued in 1993 by then prime minister Edouard Balladur is to be repaid today, market expects some 90 billion francs.
-- Federation of health practitioners sees dialogue re-established with the government, after opposing reforms designed by the previous government to curb health spending.
-- Prime Minister's office opposed to a privatisation of nuclear power builder Framatome, according to union sources.
-- Government reaffirms that the companies to be involved in the building of a new defence industry pillar around Thomson-CSF are not chosen yet.
-- Portuguese subsidiary of Credit Lyonnais to be sold to Spanish savings bank Caixa Galicia for some 300 million francs.
LA TRIBUNE
-- A wide array of financial products is to be offered to holders of Balladur bonds who seek to re-invest funds to be paid back today.
-- News-only radio station France Info poised to overtake France Inter station, which lost some 300,000 listeners, according to a Mediametrie survey.
-- Junior minister for budgetary affairs Christian Sautter said on Tuesday he expects public deficits slightly above 3.5 percent of GDP for 1997.
L'AGEFI
-- Thomson-CSF shares lost 3.6 percent on Tuesday after government announced it was halting privatisation process launched by the previous government.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- Valeo auto parts maker chairman Noel Goutard says in an interview a 35-hour working week is a delusion which may drive businesses out of the country due to higher cost of labour, adds target for Valeo is a 40-billion-franc turnover for the year 2000, with a ten-percent annual growth.
-- Luxury goods group LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault expected to present to Guinness and GrandMet tomorrow his proposals on merger.
LIBERATION (Economic section)

-- Uncertainty about the European single currency is boosting the dollar, as financial markets become skeptical about the ability of Germany and France to meet the Maastricht treaty criterion on public deficits.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Thomson shares fall after government cancels sale.
